# VoxCode Real Interview Experience Upgrade — Comprehensive Specification Analysis

**Generated by Spec Miner 0**  
**Working Directory:** `.agents/teamwork/spec_miner_0`  
**Authoritative Reference:** `REAL_INTERVIEW_UPGRADE_PLAN.md` & `ORIGINAL_REQUEST.md`  
**Codebase Baseline:** Node.js Express Backend (`backend/`), Vite React Frontend (`frontend/`), MongoDB / Mongoose

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Architecture Overview

The VoxCode Real Interview Upgrade transitions VoxCode from a turn-based REST application with robotic TTS and end-of-session evaluation into a live, bidirectional, streaming real-time interview platform indistinguishable from an actual human technical interview (comparable to ChatGPT Voice / Gemini Live in technical interview mode).

### Current vs. Target Architecture Matrix

| Dimension | Baseline State (Current Codebase) | Target State (Upgrade Specification) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Voice & Speech** | Edge/Google TTS synthesized on full turn; Browser SpeechSynthesis fallback; high latency (~4s) | Sentence-streaming Edge Neural & GCP Neural2 TTS; sub-300ms first audio packet latency; sample-accurate Web Audio playback queue |
| **Transport Protocol** | REST HTTP (`POST /api/interview/message`, `POST /api/tts/synthesize`) | Persistent WebSocket connection at `/ws/interview`; bidirectional frames for audio, text, code, and interruptions |
| **Interruption Handling** | Client-side stop of local audio only; backend continues running | Full barge-in: client detects voice activity, sends `INTERRUPT`, backend aborts LLM generation (`AbortController`), destroys TTS stream, transmits `AI_INTERRUPTED` |
| **Interviewer Persona** | Generic "Rohan" persona with static prompt | Per-company dynamically generated persona (`personaCache`), company culture directives, natural speech directives, scraped live intel |
| **Question Adaptation** | Topic progression by fixed topic count or blueprint pacing | Adaptive question difficulty engine conditioned on running Candidate Readiness Index (CRI), micro-scores, and performance signal |
| **Live Scraping & Intel** | 2-hour in-memory cache of Gemini search grounding on assessment creation | Fresh per-session multi-source scraping (Reddit, LeetCode, Glassdoor, Blind) + resume-aware question seed algorithm |
| **Evaluation Engine** | Post-session one-shot grading call | Turn-by-turn micro-scoring (0-10) + running CRI tracker (EMA $\alpha=0.4$) + 5-pass parallel deep evaluation |
| **IDE Collaboration** | Code submitted only on manual execute button | Live Monaco IDE streaming code snapshots debounced at 8s with conversational AI commentary; dual Docker / isolated child_process runner |
| **Training & Feedback** | None; static system prompts | Session training signals captured on `InterviewSession`; nightly calibration job; question bank effectiveness tracking & auto-retirement |
| **Verification & Simulation**| 62 integration tests + unit test suite | Automated simulation suite (50+ runs across 3 personas) + voice latency benchmark harness (<300ms target) |

## 2. Requirements & Acceptance Criteria Breakdown (R1 – R6)

### R1. Real-Time Voice Conversation Engine (Phase 1)
- **Feature 1.1: Persistent WebSocket Session Endpoint**
  - Mount WebSocket server at path `/ws/interview` over the main HTTP server instance.
  - Require query parameters: `token` (JWT authentication) and `sessionId` (valid `InterviewSession` ID).
  - Validation: Authenticate candidate via `jwt.verify(token, JWT_ACCESS_SECRET)`; verify that `session.candidate.toString() === decoded.id` and `session.status === 'IN_PROGRESS'`.
  - Invariants: Reject invalid JWT with WS close code `4001` (Unauthorized); reject non-existent or unauthorized session with `4003` (Session not found); reject completed or timed-out sessions with `4004` (Session already completed).
- **Feature 1.2: Client-to-Server Message Dispatch**
  - Supports framed JSON messages:
    - `TEXT_MESSAGE`: Final candidate speech transcript or text input.
    - `AUDIO_CHUNK`: Streaming base64 PCM microphone audio.
    - `CODE_SNAPSHOT`: Live Monaco IDE editor contents with language tag.
    - `INTERRUPT`: Candidate barge-in signal to cancel active AI speech.
- **Feature 1.3: Sentence-Boundary Chunking TTS**
  - Synthesize and stream speech at sentence boundaries instead of waiting for full LLM generation.
  - Sentence splitter regex: `/[^.!?]+[.!?]+(?:\s+|$)|[^.!?]+$/g`.
  - Stream chunks over WebSocket as `AUDIO_CHUNK` frames with `audioBase64` and sentence `text`.
- **Feature 1.4: Web Audio Playback Queue**
  - Frontend queue manages sequential playback of incoming audio chunks without clipping or gaps.
  - Immediate queue flush and audio buffer cancellation upon candidate interruption.
- **Feature 1.5: Hybrid Browser/Server STT**
  - Primary: Browser Web Speech API (`webkitSpeechRecognition` continuous mode with interim results).
  - Fallback: Server-side Google Cloud Speech-to-Text (`SpeechClient` streaming `LINEAR16` PCM, 16kHz sample rate, Indian English `en-IN` with US English `en-US` alternative).
- **Feature 1.6: Barge-In Interruption Handling**
  - Frontend VAD detects candidate speech while AI audio is playing; halts audio player and dispatches `INTERRUPT`.
  - Backend receives `INTERRUPT`, signals `AbortController.abort()` to terminate Gemini token stream, tears down active TTS pipeline, and broadcasts `AI_INTERRUPTED`.

### R2. Hyper-Realistic AI Interviewer Persona & Intelligence Scraping (Phases 2 & 3)
- **Feature 2.1: Per-Company Persona Builder**
  - Construct custom persona object: interviewer name, title, interview style (`direct`, `Socratic`, `whiteboard-heavy`), top focus areas, authentic question bank, and evaluation rubrics.
  - Cache persona documents in MongoDB collection `personacaches` with a 7-day TTL (`cachedAt > Date.now() - 7 days`).
- **Feature 2.2: Human Speech Directives (`HUMAN_SPEECH_DIRECTIVES`)**
  - Enforce human conversational constraints in all system prompts:
    - Mandatory contractions (`you're`, `it's`, `let's`, `I'd`).
    - Conversational acknowledgments before answering (`Yeah`, `Right`, `Gotcha`, `Interesting`).
    - Spoken thinking aloud (`Let me think about how to phrase this...`).
    - Referencing earlier conversation points (`Earlier you mentioned Redis...`).
    - Strictly forbid bullet points, numbered lists, and markdown bold in spoken output.
    - Strictly forbid robotic praise (`Great question!`, `Excellent!`).
    - Strict turn brevity: 1–4 conversational sentences per response turn.
- **Feature 2.3: Adaptive Question Difficulty Engine**
  - Dynamically read candidate performance signal (`strong`, `adequate`, `weak`, `no_answer`) and running CRI score (0–10).
  - Branching rules:
    - `strong`: Advance to harder sub-topic / complex edge cases immediately without lingering.
    - `adequate`: Probe depth with one targeted clarifying follow-up.
    - `weak`: Simplify the constraint, provide an encouraging hint, do not embarrass.
    - `no_answer`: Rephrase differently, provide architectural scaffolding.
- **Feature 2.4: Multi-Source Scraping Matrix**
  - Ground session intelligence via Google Search Grounding with targeted multi-query matrix across Reddit, LeetCode Discuss, Glassdoor, and Blind.
- **Feature 2.5: Resume-Aware Question Seed Algorithm**
  - Extract candidate projects, technologies, and past employers from uploaded resume.
  - Generate anchored questions comparing candidate's past technical decisions against the target company's architectural scale.

### R3. Empirical Benchmarking for Realism & Dialogue Design (Phase 2 & Phase 8)
- **Feature 3.1: Conversational Cadence Codification**
  - Benchmark live interviewer pacing against ChatGPT Voice & Gemini Live: target median response length of 35–45 words.
  - Implement natural time-boxing transitions based on elapsed blueprint minutes.
- **Feature 3.2: Scaffolding and Reaction Styles**
  - Emulate human pair-programming reactions during coding: acknowledging trade-offs rather than lecturing.

### R4. Real-Time Progressive Evaluation & Coding Round Upgrade (Phases 4 & 5)
- **Feature 4.1: Turn-by-Turn Micro-Scoring**
  - Grade every candidate answer turn immediately with lightweight rubric scoring (0–10) across four dimensions: `correctness`, `depth`, `communication`, `practical_application`.
  - Fast-path for non-answers (<10 chars): assign score 0 and signal `no_answer`.
- **Feature 4.2: Candidate Readiness Index (CRI) Tracker**
  - Calculate running candidate capability using Exponential Moving Average (EMA) with $\alpha = 0.4$ for topic scores.
  - Maintain rolling averages for communication score and technical depth.
  - Compute `overallSignal` (`strong` if $\ge 7.5$, `adequate` if $\ge 5.0$, else `weak`).
- **Feature 4.3: Multi-Pass Deep Final Evaluation**
  - Replace single-pass evaluation with 5 parallel evaluation passes:
    1. Topic-by-topic depth analysis
    2. Cross-topic consistency & pattern analysis
    3. Live coding quality & test verification
    4. Technical communication clarity analysis
    5. Behavioral signals & culture fit assessment
- **Feature 4.4: Live Collaborative Monaco IDE Sync**
  - Candidate editor changes stream `CODE_SNAPSHOT` frames to backend over WebSocket.
  - Debounce observation analysis at 8,000ms (8s) of typing inactivity.
  - AI generates natural 1–2 sentence peer-observation or returns an empty string if nothing notable is observed.
- **Feature 4.5: Adaptive Coding Problem Difficulty**
  - Coding problem selected dynamically matching candidate's `overallSignal`: `strong` $\to$ Hard, `adequate` $\to$ Medium, `weak` $\to$ Easy.
- **Feature 4.6: Dual Sandbox Execution (Docker + child_process)**
  - Primary execution via Docker containers with memory limits (`--memory 256m`), CPU limits (`--cpus 1.0`), and disabled network (`--network none`).
  - Automatic fallback to isolated local `child_process` execution if Docker daemon is not active.

### R5. Self-Improving Training Loop & Data Architecture (Phases 6 & 7)
- **Feature 5.1: Session Training Signal Capture**
  - Record per-question effectiveness (`candidateSignal`, `topicCoverage`, `discriminativeness`) and post-session outcomes (`hireable`, `candidateRating`, `evaluationAccuracy`) on the `InterviewSession` document.
- **Feature 5.2: Nightly Calibration Engine**
  - Automated calibration pass (`calibrateEvaluation.js`) compares AI evaluation recommendation against human hire outcomes, computes adjustment factors, and stores calibration settings.
- **Feature 5.3: Question Bank Learning Loop**
  - Automated question optimizer (`optimizeQuestionBank.js`) identifies questions with low discriminativeness ($< 0.30$) over 10+ sessions, rewrites them using LLM, and marks original questions as `retired`.
- **Feature 5.4: Dedicated Mongoose Models**
  - Register `personaCache.model.js`, `questionBank.model.js`, and `calibrationConfig.model.js`.
- **Feature 5.5: Frontend Reactive Voice Hooks**
  - Implement `useInterviewSocket.js`, `useVAD.js`, `useAudioQueue.js`, and `LiveTranscript.jsx`.

### R6. Verification and Simulation Test Harness (Phase 8)
- **Feature 6.1: Automated Interview Simulation Suite**
  - Execute 50+ end-to-end simulated interviews (`simulateInterview.js`) across three distinct synthetic candidate personas: `strong_swe`, `average_swe`, `junior_swe`.
  - Assert score boundaries: `strong_swe` $\ge 7.5$, `junior_swe` $< 5.5$.
- **Feature 6.2: Voice Latency Benchmark Harness**
  - Benchmark script (`benchmarkLatency.js`) measuring end-to-end time: input $\to$ Gemini stream $\to$ first sentence boundary $\to$ Edge TTS synthesis.
  - Assert that first audio packet latency is $< 300\text{ ms}$ and total turn response is $< 800\text{ ms}$.
- **Feature 6.3: Zero Regression Baseline**
  - All 62 existing tests in `backend/tests/integration.test.js` and all unit tests in `backend/tests/interviewEvaluation.test.js` must pass without regressions.

## 3. WebSocket Protocol Specification

### 3.1 Connection Handshake & Lifecycle

- **URL Scheme:** `ws://` (HTTP) or `wss://` (HTTPS)
- **Mount Path:** `/ws/interview`
- **Handshake Query Parameters:**
  ```
  /ws/interview?token=<JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN>&sessionId=<INTERVIEW_SESSION_ID>
  ```
- **Handshake Security Verification Sequence:**
  1. Extract `token` query param. Verify with `jwt.verify(token, process.env.JWT_ACCESS_SECRET)`. If missing or invalid, immediately terminate socket: `ws.close(4001, 'Unauthorized')`.
  2. Extract `sessionId` query param. Fetch `InterviewSession.findById(sessionId)`.
  3. Verify candidate ownership: `session.candidate.toString() === decoded.id`. If missing or mismatched: `ws.close(4003, 'Session not found')`.
  4. Verify session lifecycle status: `session.status === 'IN_PROGRESS'`. If status is `COMPLETED` or `TIMED_OUT`: `ws.close(4004, 'Session already completed')`.
  5. On successful verification, register connection in active session registry and send `SESSION_READY`.

### 3.2 Client $\to$ Server Message Schemas

#### 1. `TEXT_MESSAGE`
Used when the candidate submits a final transcript from browser speech recognition or types a response manually.
```json
{
  "type": "TEXT_MESSAGE",
  "text": "I would use a distributed Redis cluster with consistent hashing to cache session state."
}
```

#### 2. `AUDIO_CHUNK`
Used when the client streams raw microphone audio chunks for server-side processing.
```json
{
  "type": "AUDIO_CHUNK",
  "data": "UklGRiQAAABXQVZFZm10IBAAAAABAAEA...",
  "format": "LINEAR16",
  "sampleRate": 16000,
  "channels": 1
}
```

#### 3. `CODE_SNAPSHOT`
Transmitted on editor change events (debounced on client at 500ms).
```json
{
  "type": "CODE_SNAPSHOT",
  "code": "function twoSum(nums, target) {\n    const map = new Map();\n    for (let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {\n        const complement = target - nums[i];\n        if (map.has(complement)) return [map.get(complement), i];\n        map.set(nums[i], i);\n    }\n    return [];\n}",
  "language": "javascript"
}
```

#### 4. `INTERRUPT`
Dispatched immediately when client Voice Activity Detection (VAD) detects candidate speech during active AI audio playback.
```json
{
  "type": "INTERRUPT"
}
```

### 3.3 Server $\to$ Client Message Schemas

#### 1. `SESSION_READY`
Dispatched immediately upon successful WebSocket connection authentication.
```json
{
  "type": "SESSION_READY",
  "sessionId": "672251a89b4f2c0012e84120",
  "stage": "CONCEPTUAL",
  "interviewerName": "Karthik",
  "interviewerTitle": "Staff Software Engineer at Stripe",
  "currentTopic": "System Architecture & High-Throughput Ingestion"
}
```

#### 2. `TEXT_TOKEN`
Dispatched for live transcript streaming as tokens arrive from Gemini before sentence TTS completes.
```json
{
  "type": "TEXT_TOKEN",
  "token": "Definitely. ",
  "turnId": "turn_1793369201",
  "isFirst": true
}
```

#### 3. `AUDIO_CHUNK`
Dispatched as each sentence chunk is synthesized by Edge Neural TTS.
```json
{
  "type": "AUDIO_CHUNK",
  "turnId": "turn_1793369201",
  "index": 0,
  "isFinal": false,
  "text": "Definitely, that makes sense.",
  "audioBase64": "data:audio/mp3;base64,//uQxAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAWGluZwAAAA8AAAA...",
  "mimeType": "audio/mp3"
}
```

#### 4. `AI_INTERRUPTED`
Dispatched by backend acknowledging that active generation and speech have been aborted.
```json
{
  "type": "AI_INTERRUPTED",
  "turnId": "turn_1793369201"
}
```

#### 5. `AI_CODE_COMMENT`
Dispatched when background code observation produces an engineering observation during live coding.
```json
{
  "type": "AI_CODE_COMMENT",
  "text": "I see you're using a hash map for $O(n)$ lookup—good call. Keep an eye on duplicate keys if the array contains identical numbers."
}
```

#### 6. `MICRO_SCORE_UPDATE`
Dispatched after turn evaluation to update candidate readiness telemetry in real time.
```json
{
  "type": "MICRO_SCORE_UPDATE",
  "cri": 7.8,
  "overallSignal": "strong",
  "topicScores": {
    "Distributed Systems": 8.2,
    "Data Structures": 7.5
  }
}
```

#### 7. `STAGE_TRANSITION`
Dispatched when the interviewer transitions between interview stages.
```json
{
  "type": "STAGE_TRANSITION",
  "stage": "CODING",
  "codingChallenge": {
    "title": "Optimal LRU Cache Implementation",
    "difficulty": "Medium",
    "description": "Design a data structure that follows the constraints of a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache.",
    "starterCode": "class LRUCache {\n    constructor(capacity) {\n        \n    }\n}",
    "language": "javascript"
  }
}
```

#### 8. `ERROR`
Dispatched on protocol or execution errors.
```json
{
  "type": "ERROR",
  "code": "AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT",
  "message": "AI generation exceeded deadline. Please repeat your last response."
}
```

## 4. Neural Voice Engine & TTS Streaming Specification

### 4.1 Voice Model Hierarchy & Priority
High-fidelity neural TTS models must be prioritized; browser native TTS must never be chosen in WebSocket mode:
1. **Tier 1 (Default): Microsoft Edge Online Neural**
   - Voices: `en-IN-NeerjaNeural` (Female), `en-IN-PrabhatNeural` (Male).
   - Format: `AUDIO_24KHZ_48KBITRATE_MONO_MP3`.
   - Latency: ~120–160ms synthesis time per sentence.
   - Cost: $0, zero API keys required, unlimited quota.
2. **Tier 2 (Fallback): Google Cloud TTS Neural2 / WaveNet**
   - Voices: `en-IN-Neural2-B` (Male), `en-IN-Neural2-D` (Female).
   - Format: `MP3` / `LINEAR16`.
   - Trigger: Used if Edge TTS network fails or when `GOOGLE_TTS_API_KEY` is explicitly provided.
3. **Tier 3 (Emergency): Deprioritized Browser Speech**
   - Browser `SpeechSynthesis` is strictly avoided and disabled during WebSocket voice sessions to maintain audio fidelity and consistent latency.

### 4.2 Sentence Boundary Chunking Algorithm
The sentence chunking engine accumulates streaming LLM tokens into a buffer and yields complete sentences immediately for parallel synthesis:
```javascript
export async function* streamTTSChunks(tokenStream, voiceModel = 'edge-neural-neerja') {
    let sentenceBuffer = '';
    const sentenceDelimiter = /([.!?]+(?:\s+|$))/g;

    for await (const token of tokenStream) {
        sentenceBuffer += token;
        
        let match;
        // Search for sentence boundaries in buffer
        while ((match = sentenceDelimiter.exec(sentenceBuffer)) !== null) {
            const boundaryIndex = match.index + match[0].length;
            const completeSentence = sentenceBuffer.slice(0, boundaryIndex).trim();
            sentenceBuffer = sentenceBuffer.slice(boundaryIndex);
            sentenceDelimiter.lastIndex = 0; // reset regex index

            if (completeSentence.length >= 10) {
                const audioBuffer = await synthesizeEdgeSpeech(completeSentence, voiceNameFor(voiceModel));
                yield {
                    text: completeSentence,
                    audioBase64: audioBuffer.audioBase64
                };
            }
        }
    }

    // Flush any remaining characters in the buffer
    const remaining = sentenceBuffer.trim();
    if (remaining.length > 0) {
        const audioBuffer = await synthesizeEdgeSpeech(remaining, voiceNameFor(voiceModel));
        yield {
            text: remaining,
            audioBase64: audioBuffer.audioBase64
        };
    }
}
```

### 4.3 Latency Targets & Verification Math
- **Perceived Speech-to-Audio Latency Target:** $< 300\text{ ms}$ (time between candidate speech end and the first audible sound from the AI).
- **Total Turn-around Latency Target:** $< 800\text{ ms}$ (total time to synthesize and deliver sentence 1).
- **Latency Breakdown Budget:**
  - VAD End-of-Speech Detection: $\approx 80\text{ ms}$
  - WebSocket Transit: $\approx 20\text{ ms}$
  - Gemini TTFT (Time to First Token): $\approx 180\text{ ms}$
  - Sentence 1 Accumulation (3–6 words): $\approx 50\text{ ms}$
  - Edge Neural Synthesis (Sentence 1): $\approx 140\text{ ms}$
  - Audio Packet Transit + Web Audio Decode: $\approx 30\text{ ms}$
  - **First Audio Packet Delivery:** $\mathbf{\approx 280\text{ ms} < 300\text{ ms}}$.

## 5. Persona Engine & Intelligence Scraping Specification

### 5.1 Persona Engine Architecture & `personaCache` Schema

Mongoose model file: `backend/src/models/personaCache.model.js`

```javascript
import mongoose, { Schema } from 'mongoose';

const personaCacheSchema = new Schema({
    company: {
        type: String,
        required: true,
        trim: true,
        index: true
    },
    role: {
        type: String,
        required: true,
        trim: true,
        index: true
    },
    experienceLevel: {
        type: String,
        enum: ['Entry', 'Junior', 'Mid', 'Senior', 'Staff', 'Lead', 'Principal'],
        default: 'Mid'
    },
    persona: {
        name: { type: String, required: true },
        title: { type: String, required: true },
        style: { 
            type: String, 
            enum: ['direct', 'Socratic', 'whiteboard-heavy', 'systems-first', 'bar-raiser'],
            default: 'Socratic'
        },
        focusAreas: [{ type: String }],
        questionBank: [{ type: String }],
        culture: { type: String },
        rubrics: [{
            dimension: { type: String, required: true },
            description: { type: String, required: true },
            weight: { type: Number, default: 1 }
        }],
        systemPrompt: { type: String, required: true }
    },
    cachedAt: {
        type: Date,
        default: Date.now,
        index: { expires: 604800 } // TTL 7 days (7 * 24 * 3600)
    }
}, { timestamps: true });

personaCacheSchema.index({ company: 1, role: 1, experienceLevel: 1 });

export const PersonaCache = mongoose.model('PersonaCache', personaCacheSchema);
```

### 5.2 Mandatory `HUMAN_SPEECH_DIRECTIVES`
The following directives MUST be prepended to the system prompt of every interviewer persona:
```
SPEECH STYLE — STRICTLY FOLLOW:
- Use contractions naturally: "you're", "it's", "let's", "I'd", "we've", "there's".
- Acknowledge before responding: "Yeah", "Right", "Gotcha", "Interesting approach", "Makes sense".
- Think out loud occasionally: "Let me think about how that scales...", "Hmm, let's explore that corner case."
- Reference earlier points in the conversation: "Earlier you mentioned Redis — how does that tie into this queue?"
- Express genuine human engineering reactions: "Oh that's a neat pattern", "Hmm, I haven't seen that used with Kafka before."
- NEVER use markdown bullet points, numbered lists, asterisks, or bold tags in spoken responses.
- NEVER say robotic filler like "Great question!", "Excellent answer!", or "As an AI...".
- Keep responses conversational and brief: strictly 1 to 4 natural sentences per turn.
- Time-box naturally: "We've spent about ten minutes here, let's shift over to the code editor."
- React gracefully to pauses or silence: "Take your time", "No rush, think it through."
```

### 5.3 Multi-Source Scraping Query Matrix

The scraper must execute a 4-channel search query matrix using Google Search Grounding:
1. **Reddit Technical Communities:**
   `"${companyName}" "${roleTitle}" interview questions 2024 OR 2025 OR 2026 site:reddit.com/r/cscareerquestions OR site:reddit.com/r/leetcode OR site:reddit.com/r/interviewbit`
2. **LeetCode Discuss Question Leaks:**
   `"${companyName}" "${roleTitle}" interview questions site:leetcode.com/discuss 2024 OR 2025`
3. **Glassdoor & Blind Interview Debriefs:**
   `"${companyName}" engineering interview experience "${experienceLevel}" site:glassdoor.com OR site:teamblind.com`
4. **levels.fyi Hiring Bar & Architecture Loops:**
   `site:levels.fyi "${companyName}" interview process ${roleTitle}`

### 5.4 Resume-Aware Question Seed Algorithm
```javascript
export function buildResumeAwareQuestionSeeds(candidateResume, companyIntel) {
    const resumeProjects = extractProjects(candidateResume);
    const resumeTech = extractTechStack(candidateResume);
    const pastCompanies = extractCompanies(candidateResume);

    const projectQuestions = resumeProjects.slice(0, 3).map(p => 
        `You mentioned ${p.title} on your resume—walk me through the hardest architectural trade-off or failure mode you had to engineer around on that.`
    );

    const intelQuestions = (companyIntel.questionBank || [])
        .filter(q => resumeTech.some(tech => q.toLowerCase().includes(tech.toLowerCase())))
        .slice(0, 3);

    const scaleComparisonQuestions = pastCompanies.slice(0, 2).map(c => 
        `How does what you architected at ${c} compare to how you would design it to handle 100x traffic at ${companyIntel.companyName}?`
    );

    return [
        ...projectQuestions,
        ...intelQuestions,
        ...scaleComparisonQuestions
    ];
}
```

## 6. Real-Time Progressive Evaluation & Candidate Readiness Index (CRI)

### 6.1 Turn-by-Turn Micro-Scoring Protocol

- **Input Prompt Structure:**
  ```
  You are an expert technical interviewer evaluating a single answer turn.
  TOPIC: <active_topic>
  QUESTION: "<interviewer_question>"
  CANDIDATE ANSWER: "<candidate_answer>"
  RUBRICS: <rubric_dimensions_and_descriptions>
  SESSION CONTEXT: <summary_of_candidate_performance_so_far>

  Evaluate objectively. Return JSON ONLY:
  {
    "score": <number 0-10>,
    "signal": "<strong|adequate|weak|no_answer>",
    "dimensions": {
      "correctness": <number 0-10>,
      "depth": <number 0-10>,
      "communication": <number 0-10>,
      "practical_application": <number 0-10>
    },
    "keyInsight": "<one sentence summarizing the technical signal observed>"
  }
  ```
- **Guard Condition:** If candidate answer length is $< 10$ characters or empty, bypass LLM call and immediately return `{ score: 0, signal: "no_answer", dimensions: { correctness: 0, depth: 0, communication: 0, practical_application: 0 }, keyInsight: "Candidate gave no response or unintelligible input." }`.

### 6.2 Running CRI Mathematical Formulation
The Candidate Readiness Index tracks proficiency over time using an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) with $\alpha = 0.40$ to balance historical stability with immediate response quality:

$$\text{TopicScore}_k^{(t)} = 
\begin{cases} 
\text{MicroScore}, & \text{if } t = 1 \\
0.4 \cdot \text{MicroScore} + 0.6 \cdot \text{TopicScore}_k^{(t-1)}, & \text{if } t > 1 
\end{cases}$$

For global communication and technical depth dimensions:
$$\bar{D}^{(n)} = \frac{(n-1) \cdot \bar{D}^{(n-1)} + D_{\text{current}}}{n}$$

Overall Readiness Score:
$$\text{CRI}_{\text{overall}} = \frac{1}{|K|} \sum_{k \in K} \text{TopicScore}_k$$

Signal Classification:
$$\text{OverallSignal} = 
\begin{cases}
\text{"strong"}, & \text{if } \text{CRI}_{\text{overall}} \ge 7.5 \\
\text{"adequate"}, & \text{if } 5.0 \le \text{CRI}_{\text{overall}} < 7.5 \\
\text{"weak"}, & \text{if } \text{CRI}_{\text{overall}} < 5.0
\end{cases}$$

### 6.3 Multi-Pass Deep Final Evaluation Specification

At session conclusion, five parallel analytical passes are executed concurrently:
```javascript
export async function generateDeepEvaluation(session) {
    const [
        topicAnalysis,
        patternAnalysis,
        codingAnalysis,
        commAnalysis,
        behavioralAnalysis
    ] = await Promise.all([
        analyzeByTopic(session.transcript, session.microScores, session.rubrics),
        analyzeCrossTopicPatterns(session.transcript, session.microScores),
        session.codeSubmission?.code ? analyzeCodingQuality(session.codeSubmission, session.codingChallenge) : null,
        analyzeCommunicationQuality(session.transcript),
        analyzeBehavioralSignals(session.transcript)
    ]);

    return synthesizeFinalReport({
        topicAnalysis,
        patternAnalysis,
        codingAnalysis,
        commAnalysis,
        behavioralAnalysis,
        companyName: session.companyName,
        roleTitle: session.roleTitle,
        experienceLevel: session.experienceLevel
    });
}
```

## 7. Collaborative IDE & Execution Sandbox Specification

### 7.1 Live Code Observation & Debounce Logic
- Candidate keystrokes emit `CODE_SNAPSHOT` messages across the WebSocket.
- The backend maintains an in-memory observation timer per active session:
  ```javascript
  if (msg.type === 'CODE_SNAPSHOT') {
      session.liveCode = msg.code;
      clearTimeout(session.codeCommentTimer);
      session.codeCommentTimer = setTimeout(async () => {
          const observation = await generateCodeObservation(msg.code, msg.language, session);
          if (observation && observation.trim()) {
              ws.send(JSON.stringify({
                  type: 'AI_CODE_COMMENT',
                  text: observation.trim()
              }));
          }
      }, 8000); // 8-second debounce
  }
  ```
- **Code Observation Prompt Contract:**
  - Evaluates current syntax and approach choice.
  - If a clean pattern, algorithmic insight, or critical bug is emerging, returns 1–2 conversational sentences.
  - If no intervention is required, returns an empty string `""` (preventing unsolicited chat noise).

### 7.2 Adaptive Coding Challenge Selection
The coding challenge difficulty dynamically reflects candidate capability:
- `strong` $\to$ Difficulty: `Hard` (Complex DP, graph shortest paths, concurrent data structures, trie optimizations).
- `adequate` $\to$ Difficulty: `Medium` (Two pointers, binary search trees, hash table intervals, LRU cache).
- `weak` $\to$ Difficulty: `Easy` (Array traversal, string frequency maps, palindrome validation).

### 7.3 Dual Sandbox Execution Specification

#### Primary Execution: Docker Container
- Container Image: `voxcode-sandbox:latest` (or language-specific lightweight alpine runners).
- Security Constraints:
  - `--network none` (complete network isolation, preventing SSRF or exfiltration).
  - `--memory 256m` (strict 256MB RAM limit).
  - `--cpus 1.0` (strict 1-core CPU quota).
  - `--pids-limit 64` (fork-bomb mitigation).
  - `--read-only` root filesystem with isolated tmpfs mounted at `/workspace:rw,size=16m`.
  - Execution timeout: 5,000ms hard deadline.

#### Fallback Execution: Local Isolated Child Process
- If Docker is unavailable (e.g. local dev without Docker daemon running), automatically fall back to `runProcess` in `sandbox.service.js`.
- Environment variable sanitization: strip all secrets (`MONGODB_URI`, `JWT_ACCESS_SECRET`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`).
- Output buffer cap: $512\text{ KB}$ maximum buffer cap with automatic truncation warning.

#### 2. `questionBank.model.js`
Mongoose schema for tracking and retiring interview questions based on empirical discriminativeness:
```javascript
import mongoose, { Schema } from 'mongoose';

const questionBankSchema = new Schema({
    text: { type: String, required: true, unique: true },
    company: { type: String, index: true },
    role: { type: String, index: true },
    topics: [{ type: String }],
    difficulty: { type: String, enum: ['Easy', 'Medium', 'Hard'], default: 'Medium' },
    status: { type: String, enum: ['active', 'retired'], default: 'active' },
    useCount: { type: Number, default: 0 },
    avgDiscriminativeness: { type: Number, default: 0.5 },
    replacement: { type: String, default: null }
}, { timestamps: true });

export const QuestionBank = mongoose.model('QuestionBank', questionBankSchema);
```

#### 3. `calibrationConfig.model.js`
Mongoose schema for tracking nightly calibration adjustments:
```javascript
import mongoose, { Schema } from 'mongoose';

const calibrationConfigSchema = new Schema({
    type: { type: String, required: true, default: 'evaluation' },
    adjustments: {
        conceptualWeight: { type: Number, default: 0.35 },
        codingWeight: { type: Number, default: 0.30 },
        codeQualityWeight: { type: Number, default: 0.15 },
        communicationWeight: { type: Number, default: 0.20 },
        scoreOffset: { type: Number, default: 0 }
    },
    accuracy: { type: Number, default: 0 },
    updatedAt: { type: Date, default: Date.now }
}, { timestamps: true });

export const CalibrationConfig = mongoose.model('CalibrationConfig', calibrationConfigSchema);
```

### 8.2 Nightly Calibration Engine (`calibrateEvaluation.js`)
- Runs on a scheduled interval (e.g. daily cron).
- Identifies uncalibrated completed sessions with recorded human recruiter decisions (`trainingSignals.sessionOutcome.hireable`).
- Computes AI evaluation score delta against human verdict.
- Employs gradient adjustment to optimize rubric weights.
- Updates `calibrationconfigs` in MongoDB.

### 8.3 Question Bank Learning Loop (`optimizeQuestionBank.js`)
- Aggregates questions across sessions using MongoDB Aggregation Pipeline.
- Identifies questions with sample count $> 10$ and `avgDiscriminativeness < 0.30`.
- Prompts Gemini to rewrite the flawed question to make it more discriminative and probe concrete engineering trade-offs.
- Retires the weak question (`status: 'retired'`) and seeds the improved question.

## 9. Simulation & Benchmark Harness Specification

### 9.1 Automated Interview Simulation Harness (`simulateInterview.js`)
- **Objective:** Run 50+ consecutive simulated interview sessions across three synthetic personas to verify end-to-end stability, state transitions, scoring bounds, and zero unhandled exceptions.
- **Candidate Personas & Assertion Criteria:**
  1. `strong_swe`:
     - Behavioral Characteristics: Clear architectural vocabulary, optimal data structures (e.g., hash maps, heaps, segment trees), precise Big-O space/time proofs.
     - Acceptance Assertion: `overallScore >= 7.5` (or $\ge 75/100$), verdict strictly `Hire` or `Strong Hire`.
  2. `average_swe`:
     - Behavioral Characteristics: Solid fundamental grasp, occasional sub-optimal complexity, requires 1 hint before completing coding solution.
     - Acceptance Assertion: `5.0 <= overallScore < 7.5` (or $50 \le \text{score} < 75$), verdict strictly `Hire` or `Needs Improvement`.
  3. `junior_swe`:
     - Behavioral Characteristics: Vague high-level buzzwords, struggles with memory management or concurrency, leaves code incomplete or buggy.
     - Acceptance Assertion: `overallScore < 5.5` (or $< 55/100$), verdict strictly `Reject`.
- **Harness Invariants:**
  - Zero unhandled promise rejections.
  - Zero database lock deadlocks.
  - State machine correctly reaches `COMPLETED` phase within 30 turns.

### 9.2 Latency Benchmark Harness (`benchmarkLatency.js`)
- **Target Metrics:**
  - $T_0$: Input text received by handler.
  - $T_1$: Gemini first token received.
  - $T_2$: First sentence boundary detected.
  - $T_3$: Edge Neural TTS returns synthesized audio buffer for sentence 1.
  - Target Invariant: $(T_3 - T_0) < 800\text{ ms}$, with $(T_3 - T_2) < 200\text{ ms}$.

## 10. Frontend Architecture & Hook Contracts

### 10.1 `useInterviewSocket.js`
- Connects to `ws://.../ws/interview?token=...&sessionId=...`.
- Reconnects with exponential backoff on unexpected disconnect.
- Dispatches parsed incoming events to handlers: `SESSION_READY`, `AUDIO_CHUNK`, `TEXT_TOKEN`, `AI_INTERRUPTED`, `AI_CODE_COMMENT`, `STAGE_TRANSITION`.
- Exposes transmit methods: `sendTextMessage(text)`, `sendAudioChunk(base64)`, `sendCodeSnapshot(code, language)`, `sendInterrupt()`.

### 10.2 `useAudioQueue.js`
- Manages an internal Web Audio API playback pipeline (`AudioContext`, `AudioBufferSourceNode`).
- Sequentially plays queued audio chunks seamlessly without gap or click artifacts.
- Exposes `clearQueue()` which instantly stops current playback node and purges all queued buffers.

### 10.3 `useVAD.js` (Voice Activity Detection)
- Analyzes microphone stream audio levels via Web Audio `AnalyserNode`.
- When volume exceeds threshold while `isAiSpeaking === true`, immediately triggers `onBargeIn()` callback (which calls `sendInterrupt()` and `clearQueue()`).
